name: Black cabbage (food medium)
description: Food-derived medium: metabolizable components of Black cabbage (Brassica oleracea var. viridis) [Vegetables] from FooDB, plus a standard M9 mineral base. Organic components use presence-based uptake bounds; FooDB content retained. Measured compounds with no BiGG exchange are listed under uncovered.

provenance.citation: FooDB v2020-04-07 (Wishart DS et al., foodb.ca). Content sources: USDA.
provenance.notes: Organic components mapped from FooDB compounds to BiGG via InChIKey/name. Mineral base added. Bounds presence-based; foodb_content retained. Unmapped measured compounds kept in uncovered (v2 completeness fix). IMPORTANT: composition values are taken from the archived FooDB 2020-04-07 CSV data release; FooDB's live food page no longer displays this bulk composition, so it will appear empty. Verify individual compounds via the per-component cross-reference links. Underlying content was aggregated by FooDB from USDA / DTU / Phenol Explorer.
provenance.verification: expert-curated (multi-source food composition; growth-relevant profile completed, FooDB noise removed)
curation_sources: USDA FoodData Central FDC 323505 (Kale, raw, Foundation Foods) - full fresh-weight panel: proximates, individual sugars, 18 amino acids, fatty acids, minerals, vitamins, carotenoids

Ayaz et al. 2006, Food Chemistry 96:572-579, 'Nutrient contents of kale (Brassica oleraceae L. var. acephala DC.)' - explicitly 'black cabbage'; source for organic acids (citric 2213, malic 151 mg/100g dw) and free-sugar profile (fructose>glucose>sucrose)
FooDB FOOD00247 (original record; provenance for glycine betaine, molybdate, sulfate, chloride, ammonium, quercetin, lauric acid)
Kale review, Cogent Food & Agriculture 2020, doi:10.1080/23311932.2020.1811048 (organic-acid genotype ranges: citric 1962-3743, malic 454-3175 mg/100g dw)
provenance.curation_notes: Black cabbage = cavolo nero / Tuscan (Lacinato) kale, Brassica oleracea var. acephala - the exact taxon of Ayaz 2006 ('black cabbage'). It is a LOW-sugar, protein- and mineral-rich leafy brassica: dominant fermentable carbon sources are the free sugars (glucose+fructose+sucrose ~1.0 g/100g), the abundant amino acid pool (Glu, Asp, Leu, Arg lead; total protein 2.9 g/100g), and citric acid (~0.23 g/100g fresh) as the leading organic acid - the latter two were entirely absent from the FooDB record
curation_added: citric acid (dominant organic acid, ~230 mg/100g fresh)
D-fructose (0.43 g/100g) - individual sugars; FooDB had only sucrose
quantitative amounts attached to every mineral, vitamin and amino acid

curation_removed.name: D-Serine
curation_removed.reason: Wrong enantiomer: plants/kale contain L-serine, not D-serine. Almost certainly a FooDB/BiGG ID-mapping artifact. Replaced by L-serine (0.12 g/100g).

curation_removed.name: Nickel
curation_removed.reason: Non-essential trace element for the food matrix; ultra-trace contaminant, not a defining growth nutrient. FooDB predicted/soil-uptake noise.

curation_removed.name: Co2+
curation_removed.reason: Cobalt is ultra-trace and not a required plant nutrient; retained value is FooDB predicted noise rather than a measured growth-relevant amount. (Cobalt matters only via B12, which kale lacks.)

curation_removed.name: CO2 CO2
curation_removed.reason: Gas-exchange metabolite of the model environment, not a food-derived nutrient of black cabbage. Belongs to the aerobic medium boundary, not the composition.

curation_removed.name: O2 O2
curation_removed.reason: Model boundary gas (aerobic exchange), not a food nutrient. Provided by the medium environment, not the leaf.

curation_removed.name: H+
curation_removed.reason: Proton/charge-balance exchange metabolite, not a food composition nutrient.

curation_removed.name: Iron (Fe3+) / Fe2+ mitochondria
curation_removed.reason: Redundant duplicate iron entries (three FooDB iron rows). Consolidated into a single measured 'iron' 1.6 mg/100g; the compartment-tagged 'Fe2+ mitochondria' is a model artifact.

coverage_source.definition: pct_covered_all divides components by (components + unresolved ingredients). It counts pipeline-derived components as covered, so it is not a measure of how much of the source's own ingredient list was captured. pct_covered_source divides source-stated components by (those + unresolved ingredients + ingredients replaced by derived components), which is that measure. Component classes come from tools/component_evidence_classes.tsv. A null value means the denominator was zero; it does not mean 100.
